$comment: Rule catalog — deployment. Standards 23, 25. The contract the model presents at prediction time, and the document that travels with it. deployment.model-card carries the only detector in this category, and it checks for a document with the right headings — never for whether the limitations it states are the model's actual limitations.

rules.title: A model card documents the model and its limitations
rules.description: A model card records what the model does, its intended use, the data it was trained on, its evaluation including segment-level results, and what it does not do — and travels with the model wherever its outputs are used.
rules.rationale: The people who consume a model's outputs are rarely the people who built it, and the assumptions that make the outputs meaningful are invisible at the point of use. A card is where those assumptions become available to someone who was not there.
rules.remediation: Add a MODEL_CARD.md covering model details, intended use, training data, evaluation with a baseline and a segment breakdown, calibration, and limitations. The templates directory ships a conforming example.
rules.evidenceExpected: A model card carrying at minimum an intended-use section, an evaluation section, and a limitations section.
rules.$assuranceNote: The check looks for a model-card document or the corresponding headings, and headings only — a heading is a structural claim, a word occurrence in prose is a mention. It verifies that a card with the expected sections exists; whether the limitations stated are the model's actual limitations is human judgement, and a limitations section listing only what was already obvious to its author would pass this check unchanged.

rules.title: The inference contract is specified and matches training
rules.description: The model's behaviour at prediction time is written down — input contract, preprocessing, output shape and meaning, thresholds, latency, and behaviour on missing or malformed input — and the transformations it applies are the ones training applied.
rules.rationale: Training and serving that apply different transformations produce a model that is correct in neither, and the discrepancy does not raise an error: both paths run, and the columns silently disagree. Failure behaviour deserves the same specification as success, because a prediction path that substitutes a default for a missing feature is making an undisclosed decision.
rules.remediation: Write the contract, and share the fitted transformation artifact between training and serving rather than reimplementing it on each side.
rules.evidenceExpected: An inference specification covering inputs, transformations, outputs, thresholds, latency, and failure behaviour, plus an attestation that serving applies the training transformations.
rules.$assuranceNote: Nothing automated establishes this. Training-serving skew is a disagreement between a repository and a deployed system, and only one of the two is present to be read.
